text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bunds and futures surrendered to weakness in late trade, failing to find buyers despite 10-year cash yields trading over 6.00 percent for most of the day. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.23, down 0.19 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts remained stubbornly rangebound, with most players reluctant to take out positions ahead of Friday's U.S. payroll figures. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-13/32, down 06/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures suffered with German Bund futures amid continued uncertainty ahead of the key U.S. jobs figures on Friday, strong German data and an ongoing reluctance of French investors to take new positions. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.16, down 0.24 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets returned to positive territory by the close, helped by interest at the short end of the market and encouraged by the strengthening lira. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 124.75, up 0.33 from Wednesday's settlement price.
UNITED STATES - The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-19/32, up 01/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.08 percent.

JAPAN - Key June Japanese government bond futures ended the Tokyo session slightly lower. The key contract closed down 0.04 at 126.58. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.52, down 0.16 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - New issues dealers said they were looking to next week for some jumbo dollar deals to surface after the outcome of the U.S. jobs data on Friday. There was talk of the Asian Development Bank, European Investment Bank, Fannie Mae and World Bank eyeing long-dated dollar deals. Others said Portugal and Thailand were also eyeing the dollar sector. Details on Ecuador's dollar deal firmed up following Wednesday's roadshow in London. In sterling, ASDA set a 200 million stg 10-year bond which will be priced to yield 65 basis points over gilts.
